Issued at 353 AM EST Tue Nov 10 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Generally progressive flow across the US attm...with upper ridge 
axis centered near/just east of the Rockies and troughing generally 
over the Eastern US in the northern stream of the flow, though 
there is some ridging ahead of the PV max diving through the 
Upper Great Lakes this morning. In the southern stream, closed 
low stalled out over TX. Additional energy churning its way into
the western US/PacNW given strong jet out across the Pacific. 
Over the CONUS...100+kt upper jet stretches from the Dakotas 
down into the Great Lakes; a secondary jet max noted over the 
Yoop this morning along the BCZ aloft with that deeper 500mb 
shortwave (tropopause dipping down toward 400-500mb as the wave 
crosses Lake Superior)...and height falls are amplifying with 
this latter feature over Lake Superior and southern Ontario. 
Some mid-level moisture pooling along/ahead of the wave and 
attendant cold front stretching from the UP back into the 
Central Plains (even a touch of weak stability aloft over 
western Ontario), though quite a bit of dry air below 700mb on 
our 0z/10 sounding...and not surprised that not much has reached
the ground across our area (more abundant radar returns are 
well into Ontario as of 5z). NW-SE oriented low-level BCZ 
tightening up over central Canada attm...but still some cold 
advection into the Upper Great Lakes on a NW 30-40kt 850mb jet. 
Some very subtle moisture advection on SW flow ahead of the 
front across N Lower...but already seeing winds turn around to 
the W across WI as of 6z. 

Troughing over eastern Canada looks to retrograde this week as lobe 
of energy currently over the PacNW exits the ridge a bit early and 
digs into the Mid MS Valley Wednesday. Attm, center of the closed 
low will be in the vicinity of the Great Lakes/Ontario for the 
remainder of the workweek...only slowly exiting stage right going 
into this weekend and early next week as another round of troughing 
digs into the western US and generally forces the ridge to build 
eastward into the MS Valley/Midwest again...while also sending some 
energy through the ridge axis across the central US. Bottom 
line...cold (seasonable) air is coming...and with it, shots of lake 
effect shower activity until high pressure can build in enough to 
sufficiently squelch lake activity again, though this may take 
quite a bit of time, especially this time of year with the lakes
still around +10-12C. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Showers return Wednesday, with lake effect showers for the rest of 
the week...Not impossible we could see some NW/WNW-flow lake effect 
showers today/tonight, as temps aloft should be sufficient to 
produce overlake instability...though we should see increasing 
subsidence aloft as the jet max moves into the Lower Great Lakes and 
New England. Best shot of any showers will be across the EUP and Tip 
of the Mitt where low-level moisture is a bit more notable, esp this 
afternoon and into this evening, and especially if a subtle boundary 
draping in is able to fire anything off. Slug of mid-level moisture 
looks to arrive late tonight into Wednesday morning ahead of that 
lobe of energy tracking through the Mid MS Valley/Midwest, and 
expect this is when better chances will start to increase, sometime 
after 6-9z. Think lake enhancement is a good bet with this system, 
noting temps aloft will change very little during the day, and 
continue to fall Wednesday night with a reinforcing blow of northern 
stream energy digging in. Appears there could be some funky sort of 
inverted surface trough in our part of the region as the primary 
surface low passes to our southwest, which suggests some uncertainty 
in wind direction and subsequent focus for lake enhancement...but 
could otherwise serve as a focus for convergence...during the day 
Wednesday. Not impossible some flakes could mix in with onset of 
precip Wednesday morning as there should be some evaporative cooling 
(if it doesn't entirely nix the precip chances initially), but think 
this round will be primarily rain. 

Wednesday night, winds turn around to the north and generally remain 
from the north through the next few days, focusing lake effect 
shower potential along our coasts into the weekend, if not beyond. 
Think the best chance of mixing with or transitioning over to all 
snow will be after 0z Thursday, and esp after 6z Thursday, as temps 
at the surface fall further to allow flakes to survive a little 
better...though not impossible it could start a little sooner, 
especially in the interior higher terrain.

Accumulating snow Thursday night...already persistent north flow 
lake effect will be enhanced as some deeper moisture pivots down 
into the area behind a secondary trough that will bring even cooler 
air into the region. This idea suggests a better shot at snow, and 
potentially accumulating snow for some areas where bands stick 
around for several hours. Signals for some
